Several other RFCs, such as 131, 152 and 156, are replies with status reports.

subtitle: The chair's plan for running the May 1971 Network Working Group meeting in Atlantic City.

tldr.problem: The chair wanted to use the group's time at the Atlantic City meeting more effectively.
tldr.mechanism: Organize the meeting around advertised topics in three phases, with status reports and position papers published beforehand.
tldr.outcome: Reports and position papers were to be published in RFC form by 1 May 71, and an agenda was to follow about 1 May. It updates RFC 99.

today: RFC 116 is a record of a meeting plan, not a protocol. It updates RFC 99 and was updated by RFC 131 and RFC 156.

sections.title: The Three-Phase Plan
sections.content:
To use time in Atlantic City more effectively, the author proposes organizing the meetings around discussions of advertised topics, supported by published status reports and position papers. The time is divided into three phases.

Phase one covers status reports and introductions, phase two covers current network-wide topics, and phase three considers new topics.
sections.eli5: The meeting has three parts, like a school day with show-and-tell, group projects and new ideas.

sections.title: Phases One and Two
sections.content:
Phase one is for status reports from each site and introductions of new sites or agencies. Existing sites report on software and hardware development and their use of the network; new sites present their plans. Work on the ILLIAC IV, the List machine and the terminal IMP is also reviewed. Each site is assumed to need 5-10 minutes, and a short written status report is expected.

Phase two discusses network-wide topics such as the NIC, the Form Machine Telnet and the Logger Protocol. Committees prepare reports, and viewpoints not covered by a committee should be explained in position papers.
sections.eli5: First each group says what it has been building. Then everyone talks about the shared projects.

sections.title: Phase Three and Preparation
sections.content:
Phase three considers new topics, such as the long-range goals of the group, operational goals for the next six months, and whether the group should have more or less structure. Suggestions are encouraged and are best introduced with a position paper.

The effectiveness of the meeting depends on written material being available beforehand, so reports and position papers should be published in RFC form by 1 May 71. The agenda will be built from suggestions sent to the author and published, with a schedule, about 1 May.
sections.eli5: Last, people suggest new ideas. Everything should be written down and shared before the meeting so no time is wasted.
